-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
/-- Standard Euclidean algorithm on natural numbers. -/
def euclid (a b : Nat) : Nat :=
  if h : b = 0 then a else euclid b (a % b)
decreasing_by exact Nat.mod_lt _ (Nat.pos_of_ne_zero h)

theorem euclid_eq_gcd (a b : Nat) : euclid a b = Nat.gcd a b := by
  induction b using Nat.strong_induction_on generalizing a with
  | _ b ih =>
    rw [euclid]
    split
    · next h => subst h; simp
    · next h =>
      rw [ih (a % b) (Nat.mod_lt _ (Nat.pos_of_ne_zero h))]
      rw [Nat.gcd_comm b (a % b), ← Nat.gcd_rec, Nat.gcd_comm]

theorem gcd_le_max (a b : Nat) : Nat.gcd a b ≤ max a b := by
  rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos b with hb | hb
  · subst hb; simp
  · exact le_trans (Nat.gcd_le_right a hb) (le_max_right a b)
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definitions
def compute_gcd (a : UInt64) (b : UInt64) (h_precond : compute_gcd_precond a b) : UInt64 :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  UInt64.ofNat (euclid a.toNat b.toNat)
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def compute_gcd_postcond (a : UInt64) (b : UInt64) (result : UInt64) (h_precond : compute_gcd_precond a b) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  result.toNat = Nat.gcd (UInt64.toNat a) (UInt64.toNat b)
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem compute_gcd_postcond_satisfied (a : UInt64) (b : UInt64) (h_precond : compute_gcd_precond a b) :
    compute_gcd_postcond a b (compute_gcd a b h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  have hlt : Nat.gcd a.toNat b.toNat < 2 ^ 64 := by
    refine lt_of_le_of_lt (gcd_le_max _ _) ?_
    rcases max_cases a.toNat b.toNat with ⟨h, _⟩ | ⟨h, _⟩ <;> rw [h]
    · exact a.toNat_lt_size
    · exact b.toNat_lt_size
  simp only [compute_gcd, compute_gcd_postcond, euclid_eq_gcd]
  exact UInt64.toNat_ofNat_of_lt' hlt
  -- !benchmark @end proof

`LEAN VERIFIED` — the proof compiles with only benign unused-variable warnings, and no `sorry`/axioms.

## Approach

**Implementation** (`auxcode` + `code`): a genuine recursive Euclidean algorithm on `Nat`,

```lean
def euclid (a b : Nat) : Nat :=
  if h : b = 0 then a else euclid b (a % b)
decreasing_by exact Nat.mod_lt _ (Nat.pos_of_ne_zero h)
```

with termination by `b` decreasing under `%`. `compute_gcd` runs it on `a.toNat`, `b.toNat` and wraps the result back with `UInt64.ofNat`.

**Correctness**, in three steps:

1. `euclid_eq_gcd : euclid a b = Nat.gcd a b` — strong induction on `b` generalizing `a`. Base case `b = 0` is `Nat.gcd_zero_right`; the step uses the IH at `a % b`, then `Nat.gcd_comm` + `Nat.gcd_rec` to turn `gcd b (a % b)` into `gcd a b`.
2. `gcd_le_max : Nat.gcd a b ≤ max a b` — case split on `b = 0` (gcd is `a`) versus `b > 0` (`Nat.gcd_le_right`). The split is needed because `Nat.gcd_le_right` requires positivity, and `a = b = 0` is a real edge case.
3. The postcondition then needs no wraparound: `gcd ≤ max a b < 2^64`, so `UInt64.toNat_ofNat_of_lt'` gives `(UInt64.ofNat (gcd ..)).toNat = gcd ..` exactly.

The one thing I had to look up rather than derive was the name of that last lemma; I spent a check round on `#check`/`exact?` probes to find `UInt64.toNat_ofNat_of_lt'`, then removed the probes. Final state: 3 of 15 compiler checks used, and only `Solution.lean` was modified, within the four marker regions.
